identity.title: Towards Sub-Second Molecular Docking as a Structural Primitive: A Quantized Consistency Diffusion Framework

problem.claim: Molecular docking must provide accurate structural feedback fast enough for high-frequency, agent-driven drug-discovery loops.

gap.claim: Existing high-fidelity docking and co-folding models are constrained by iterative generative refinement and heavy computation.

contributions.claim: A compute-efficient co-folding framework combining Progressive Consistency Regularization for few-step diffusion inference with Residual-Safe Quantization for selective low-precision computation.
Information-level-matched accuracy evaluation, separating blind comparisons from blind generative methods and interface-informed comparisons from surface- or interface-informed baselines.
A docking model designed to function as a sub-second structural primitive for agent-centered drug discovery.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a framework that combines reconstruction-anchored consistency tuning with residual-safe quantization to turn docking into a sub-second structural primitive.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art docking accuracy under the matched interface-informed protocol.
The authors separately report blind-docking performance under the matched blind protocol.
For a representative 256-token complex, the model generates five conformations in 0.17 seconds on one NVIDIA H20 GPU, reported as over 300× faster than AlphaFold3 under the benchmarked setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Agent-centered discovery requires accurate domain models that are callable in real time.
Molecular docking supplies important structural feedback but is slowed by iterative refinement and heavy computation.
The proposed framework combines few-step consistency diffusion with selective quantization that protects residual streams and geometry-sensitive operations.
Accuracy is evaluated with information-level-matched protocols, alongside reported sub-second generation and a benchmarked speed comparison.
The authors frame the results as moving docking toward a real-time structural primitive.

source_observation.claim: The abstract matches comparisons to the structural-information level available to each docking method, separating blind and interface-informed protocols.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the comparison framing more explicit and reduces ambiguity about whether methods received comparable structural information.
lessons.application: When comparing systems with different inputs or priors, define matched evaluation strata and report each stratum separately.
lessons.exception: This structure is unsuitable when all methods consume genuinely identical information and no meaningful protocol distinction exists.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links each efficiency goal to a specific mechanism: consistency tuning reduces diffusion steps, while quantization selectively targets compute-intensive transformations and preserves geometry-sensitive paths in BF16.

lessons.interpretation: Mechanism-to-outcome mapping helps readers connect an engineering claim to its proposed source.
lessons.application: For an efficiency contribution, pair each claimed bottleneck reduction with the component intended to produce it and state protected operations or constraints.
lessons.exception: Avoid this decomposition when the abstract lacks evidence or the system’s effects cannot be meaningfully attributed to individual components.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide numerical accuracy values, datasets, sample counts, variance, or details of the matched protocols.
The speed result is for one representative 256-token complex and a benchmarked setting; broader runtime scope and comparison conditions are unspecified.
No ablation evidence is supplied for the separate effects of PCR and Residual-Safe Quantization.
